Communication, consideration, accountability, and reliability.
Being able to freely communicate with your partner builds trust.
Being considerate of your partner, the things they go through, their needs and wants; builds connection.
Allowing yourself to be held accountable and holding your partner accountable helps strengthen bonds by maintaining expectations. You and your partner are a team with a goal. That goal may just be just being happy together, but it still requires effort from everyone involved. Allowing your partner to tell you when you’re slacking on those goals, and being able to communicate to your partner when they have, without it turning into a blame-fest, is very important.
Being there for your partner and the being there for you is, in my opinion, the most important part of the relationship. Where you know someone is always going to show up for you. Even when they’re mad. Even when they’re tired. Relationships start to sour when a person finds that they cannot rely on their partner. It doesn’t matter what it is. If they cannot rely on you for attention, help, closeness, or support, your bond will become weaker with every instance until it breaks; and once broken it’s extremely hard to impossible to repair. 
Additionally, I learned this the hard way. I gave my all to someone who wasn’t being honest with me. I kept second-guessing myself, thinking I was being too sensitive. But deep down, I knew something was wrong. When communication didn’t give me the answers, I reached out to a discreet private investigator to confirm the truth.
